findings.claim: The corrected claim-next queue query ranks legal_priority correctly (CASE level_2=2/level_1=1 DESC with protocolled_at/id ASC ties, filters/lock/tenant preserved) but its 'else 0' branch keeps NULL and unknown legacy tokens ELIGIBLE for claiming at rank 0. ADR-0024 in this frozen readset is explicit that legal_priority = null means 'não apurado', that such cases are 'excluído do claim-next automático até saneamento' (Decisão, lines 40-42; emenda, lines 107-109), and that legacy null cases 'exigem migração definida e auditável antes do consumo automático' (lines 193-195). Because the pre/enforce upgrade deliberately never rewrites legacy legal_priority values and no migration exists in this candidate, every legacy DISTRIBUIDO case with null or an unknown string (e.g. the frozen 'legacy_unmapped_task0028') would be automatically consumed as if it were 'none' at the sole consumption point, converting the un-apurado acervo in exactly the way the pinned Owner decision forbids. Post-apply new cases are unaffected (the deferred trigger guarantees a non-null projection), so this manifests precisely on the upgraded-legacy path this rehearsal exists to prove.
findings.fix: Add an eligibility predicate to the candidate query, e.g. `and item.legal_priority in ('none','level_1','level_2')`, keeping the rank CASE and tiebreaks, so NULL and unknown legacy tokens are excluded from automatic claim-next until an audited legacy migration is delivered; run this as a new delimited Inspector RED (updated unit sensor, new frozen SHA) followed by a single-file Engineer GREEN before any DB rehearsal consumes the queue.

findings.claim: The independent claim-next sensor (real captured SQL, RED 34/35 pre-fix, GREEN 35/35 post-fix, SHA 05cbba71… unchanged across TASK-0034/0035 as recorded) pins only the ORDER BY rank expression and its comment asserts 'RN-RAIT-141: NULL and unknown legacy tokens receive rank 0', codifying claim-eligibility for não-apurado cases that ADR-0024 excludes from automatic claim-next; the sensor therefore stays GREEN on the non-conforming behavior in the high above and mis-attributes the rank-0-eligible semantics to RN-RAIT-141 when the governing frozen decision is ADR-0024.
findings.fix: When the service is corrected, extend this test (new SHA, genuine RED first) to additionally require the WHERE-clause eligibility filter for legal_priority in ('none','level_1','level_2') and correct the comment to cite ADR-0024's exclusion of null/unknown from automatic claim-next; keep SQL-level ordering proof reserved for the later dedicated-DB gate.

findings.claim: The fixture guard verifies current_database/current_user/datdba but never verifies that the session can bypass the FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY tenant_isolation policy that 11-auth-functions.sql lines 53-59 install on ops.parameter (15-ops-parameter.sql line 39). The script sets no app.tenant_id and the tenant trigger is not implicated (it fires only ON INSERT OR UPDATE OF tenant_id), so if 'aarusso' lacks superuser/BYPASSRLS the cardinality SELECT reads zero rows and the recipe aborts fail-closed — safe, but the recipe as written can only ever succeed under an unverified privilege assumption, and the before/after other-row md5 digests silently cover only RLS-visible rows rather than provably all rows.
findings.fix: Add to the guard an explicit assertion that the executing role bypasses RLS, e.g. raise unless EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user AND (rolsuper OR rolbypassrls)), and record that check plus the row-visibility count in the fresh pre-execution snapshot mandated by the recipe, so the preimage-hash and unrelated-row-preservation evidence demonstrably covers the whole table.
